steps.body: Eleven and twelve are the tricky teens: their names hide the ten. No “teen” sound — yet 11 and 12 still write ten-and-one, ten-and-two.
steps.narration: Eleven and twelve are the tricky teens: their names hide the ten. No “teen” sound — yet 11 and 12 still write ten-and-one, ten-and-two.

widget.prompt: Start at 10 and count on 2. Tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 11 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 12.
13 goes one complete hop too far. Count just 2 hops from 10 to land on 12.

widget.missFeedback: Count 2 on from 10: you land on 12.
widget.successFeedback: 10 and 2 more is 12 — the teen numeral writes exactly that: 1 ten, 2 ones.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — all 2 counts past ten are needed to reach 12.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count-on stops after 2 numbers, on 12.

predict.prompt: Does eleven contain a full ten, though its name hides it?
predict.reveal: The name is irregular but the numeral is honest: the leading 1 reports the ten.

cml.actionGoal: Link the written numeral to the exact amount it names for kcw write 11 12.
invariants: A numeral is a written promise about an amount: it records the last word of a careful count, position gives each digit its job, and the promise survives any change of objects or arrangement — the anchor for kcw write 11 12.
misconceptions: Treating numerals as decorations, reading digit pairs without position, or matching a numeral to roughly rather than exactly its amount.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more thing joined the group, which single mark of the numeral would have to change?

widget.prompt: 12 and 21 use the same two digits. Same number?

options.label: No — position gives each digit its job
options.feedback: Correct — in 12 the 1 is a ten; in 21 the 2 is two tens. Order is meaning.

options.label: Yes — same digits, same number
options.feedback: Swap the digits and the tens digit changes: twelve becomes twenty-one.

options.label: Only on Tuesdays
options.feedback: Place value never takes a day off; position always assigns the jobs.

options.label: 12 is bigger
options.feedback: 21 holds two full tens against 12's one — the swap made it BIGGER.

options.feedback: Correct — the numeral 12 is the written name for a group of exactly 12.
